value.body: The Archaeological Survey of India, under the Ministry of Culture, protects and conserves nationally important monuments and sites, runs excavations and site museums, and manages epigraphy and research. Careers range from archaeologists and conservation staff to ministerial and field posts.

items.label: Centrally protected monuments and sites
items.source: Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha replies

items.label: Training
items.note: Run by ASI's Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, Greater Noida

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Archaeologist posts usually need a master's degree in archaeology, ancient Indian history or a related subject, and often a PG diploma in archaeology; they are typically filled through UPSC recruitment advertisements. Clerical and multi-tasking posts come through SSC exams, and some field posts through ASI's own notifications.

value.title: At a glance
items: Archaeologist vacancies are small in number and not notified every year.
Field postings can be in remote sites, with travel and outdoor work.
Related paths include state archaeology departments, museums, archives and university research.
